prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1305; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at an intersection was reported by the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and states that the other vehicle entered the intersection while the claimant had the right of way.

Entry 2: Police report on file confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The driver of the claimant's vehicle lives with the policyholder and is listed as a covered household member under the policy.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene confirm the general position of both vehicles and the point of contact on the driver's side. No independent witnesses have been identified, so the account rests on the parties and the police documentation.

Entry 4: Damage to the vehicle is mostly in line with the described impact. A few old scratches near the rear quarter panel may predate this crash and are being noted separately for the estimate.

Entry 5: Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage start date. Underwriting records were reviewed and show no prior claims on the vehicle.

Entry 6: The claimant later provided a few additional details about the seating position and the moment of impact, but the core account has remained the same across each statement taken so far.

Entry 7: The reported shoulder injury matches the kind and force expected from a side impact of this type. Medical records show a usual course of treatment that tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 8: Medical history shows the claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years. That prior condition appears to add to the current complaints, and the medical reviewer is weighing its contribution separately from the crash-related injury.

Entry 9: Overall the injury and vehicle damage fit the reported collision, with the prior shoulder condition and older scratches flagged for separate handling. The file is ready for the next settlement review step.
